title: Don
summary: Consumer Reports 2012 response to the Stanford review arguing organic still lowers pesticide and antibiotic exposure, has some nutrient advantages, is better for the environment and is worth buying for high-residue foods, especially for children and pregnancy.

assertions.quote: higher levels of phosphorous and phenols (a type of antioxidant compound) in organic produce
more omega-3 fatty acids in organic milk and chicken
conventionally produced chicken and pork had a 33 percent higher risk for bacteria that's known to be resistant to at least three antibiotics
organic diets provide less exposure to pesticides and antibiotics
organic agriculture is better for the environment
Those choices are especially important for pregnant women and children.
consumers shouldn't be misled into believing that there isn't a benefit to paying more for organics, particularly for certain populations
The study downplays the importance of the prohibition of antibiotics in organic agriculture
